reason: The text portrays several elite figures unfavorably: Goliath (the Philistine elite warrior-champion) is depicted as arrogant, blasphemous, and contemptuous, defying Israel's armies with pride; Eliab (David's older brother and part of the military elite) is shown as unjustly angry toward David, misinterpreting his motives with accusations of pride and evil intent; and implicitly, the military elite's fear and inability to confront Goliath (וַיֵּחַתּוּ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד - 'they dismayed and feared greatly') contrasts with the triumph of the non-elite young shepherd David. The narrative structure emphasizes the weakness and inadequacy of established authority figures while elevating the humble outsider.
